citation.title: Minimum Wages and Employment: A Case Study of the Fast-Food Industry in New Jersey and Pennsylvania

worker_question: 1992年紐澤西州提高最低工資，如何影響當地速食餐廳的就業？
source_status: All article targets below are visually checked published values, not author-program output or a curator rerun.

primary_sources.note: 26-page file: published article pp.772-793 followed by citation pages; do not copy full text into repository

rights.data: No explicit open-data license was found in landing page, README, codebook, or archive. Public download availability is verified; redistribution rights are not inferred.
rights.article: Author-hosted published article; no blanket open license inferred. A separate author-hosted JSTOR copy includes personal/non-commercial-use terms. Keep article in temporary holdout only.

archive.version_note: README describes book Myth and Measurement chapter 2; archive timestamps are 1996-1997. Treat this public-data vintage separately from published numerical targets.
archive.readme_discrepancy: README says five files; actual archive contains six including read.me.

files.name: codebook
files.encoding_note: contains DOS box-drawing bytes; not valid UTF-8

files.name: read.me
files.role: archive description; identifies book and linked datasets

archive.code_contamination: check.sas constructs FTE employment, changes, wage-gap exposure, NJ wage groups, meal prices, and samples; directly tabulates Table 2, part of Table 3, Table 4 and unpublished proportional-change models. Reading it reveals analysis decisions even without article access.
archive.program_discrepancy: check.sas line 160 excludes CO_OWNED from its region-controlled wage-gap model, whereas published Table 4(v) includes ownership controls. Do not equate this script's output with the published target.

design.event: NJ minimum wage 4.25 to 5.05 on 1992-04-01; PA unchanged
design.sample: 410 establishments:331 NJ,79 PA; four fast-food chains
design.estimand: employment change at existing establishments; entry requires separate evidence
design.outcome: FTE = full-time nonmanager workers + managers/assistant managers + 0.5*part-time workers
design.closure_rule: permanent closures:post employment zero; temporary closures:missing in base case
design.identification: cross-state before/after difference; complementary within-NJ initial-wage comparisons
design.locators: pp.773-778; Table 1 p.774; employment construction p.775; Section III pp.778-784

published_targets.units: coefficients in FTE unless labelled proportional; standard errors in se fields

table4.sample_rule: employment change and initial wage available; second wage available or establishment permanently closed
table4.inference_note: Published standard errors are conventional OLS model standard errors; worker may add alternative inference but must label it.

table5_key_robustness.proportional_definition_locator: p.782 footnote 18; change divided by mean employment, permanent-closure change set to -1
table5_key_robustness.published_internal_difference: Table 4(ii) prints se=1.20; Table 5(row1,i) prints se=1.19 for same reported beta=2.30. Keep both; allow a rounding/source discrepancy in evaluation.

published_targets.direction: Employment reduction is not supported in the main survey estimates; positive point estimates should not be converted into an unqualified causal claim.

secondary_locators.table6: p.786 (PDF15):full-time share, hours, registers, benefits, wage progression

scope_limits: Two survey waves cannot empirically test pretreatment parallel trends; comparisons of high-wage NJ stores supplement but do not prove this assumption.
public.dat contains no ZIP code. Exact Table 5 Newark/Camden subsamples (rows10/11) need unverified extra location input.

Archive lacks Table 8 state restaurant-directory and wage inputs and Section VII monthly CPS inputs. These blocks require separate acquisition; a survey-only run cannot claim full-article numerical replication.
Original certainty about standard-error construction or historical data vintage is not implied by a successful current-code rerun.

evaluation_rules.published_vs_computed: Published targets remain immutable. Any independently computed values belong in a separate comparison file with dataset hash, transformations, estimation code and inference convention.
evaluation_rules.numeric_rounding: Compare to the displayed precision: approximately 0.005 for two-decimal coefficients, allowing explicit documented vintage or publication inconsistencies.
must_check: at least three substantively different robustness checks
do_not_reward: matching remembered headline without executable estimates
copied coefficient with no result binding
pretreatment trend claims from only two waves
asserting complete replication of missing blocks
evaluation_rules.archive_access_audit: Worker must log archive inventory before extraction and record whether check.sas or any paper/results/third-party replication was opened. Acquisition is not itself proof that analysis code was read; distinguish discovered presence from access.
evaluation_rules.memory_limit: The topic plus place/year is readily identifiable and famous. Prohibiting paper access reduces retrieval contamination but cannot establish absence of model-training memory. Treat success as constrained reconstruction, not discovery.
